catalog_quote: 2.2. The external data for Yulbaridja, as well as its phoneme inventory, are listed at the beginning of this section. This dialect is numbered 474 on Greenway's map. The general statements there made on interphonemic specification in Western Desert dialects are amplified for Yulbaridja below. ... The syllable has canonical shapes CV and CVC. ... Within the word but across morpheme boundaries, additional possibilities of clustering exist (especially in reduplications), as /pm rl/. Vowels occur medially and finally only. Stress is predictable and, as in most other Australian languages, occurs on the initial syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Yulparija (Yulbaridja) is non-contrastive and falls on the first syllable of the word.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary or rhythmic stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the word (structural sketch; 'stress is predictable'); no discussion of phrase-level prominence or clitics. The same fascicle says of neighbouring Wanman (p.136), whose phonotactics are stated to be identical to Yulbaridja's, 'Word stress is on the initial syllable -- hence predictable.'
new_statements.identity_note: O'Grady's 'Yulbaridja' (Greenway no. 474; his own 1950s field data from the La Grange/Wallal area) is the same variety as Glottolog yulp1239 Yulparija (AIATSIS A67), a northern Western Desert (Wati) dialect now spoken at Bidyadanga. Note Glottolog also files Burridge 1996 'Yulparija sketch grammar' under Martu Wangka [mart1256]; the catalog should keep the Yulparija statement separate from the Mantjiltjara/Martu Wangka entry (Marsh 1969).
